audit.title: Real World Asset (RWA) Data Streams

dimensions.name: Answer-first extractability
dimensions.analysis: The implied question ("which RWA streams exist and what are their IDs?") is answered by a table that shows `Loading...` — no liftable answer exists in static HTML. Opening line redirects to a tutorial instead of stating what the page provides.

dimensions.name: Structural scannability & chunkability
dimensions.analysis: Clean heading hierarchy, 0 level skips — but sections median 12 words and the core table never materializes server-side, so there is nothing coherent to chunk.

dimensions.name: Concrete statistics & specifics
dimensions.analysis: Weakest-in-class for a data page: 2 numerals, 0 with units, 0 hex identifiers. A stream directory should be dense with stream IDs, decimals, and 0x verifier addresses; none are present in the served content.

dimensions.name: Citations & authoritative references
dimensions.analysis: 5 internal links (discovery endpoint, LINK contracts, supported networks) are relevant and appropriate; no external primary sources needed here. Adequate.

dimensions.name: Quotable canonical definitions
dimensions.analysis: No one-sentence definition of "RWA Data Streams" or what "24/5 Equity Streams" means. Nothing verbatim-liftable.

dimensions.name: Machine-readability & metadata
dimensions.analysis: JSON-LD parses (both blocks valid), canonical + `inLanguage` set. But `datePublished`==`dateModified` (no genuine freshness signal), `keywords` are tokenized fragments ("list, available, Data..."), and `about` entries are template junk ("Content about real", "Content about world") that split "Real World Asset" into meaningless Things — actively harmful for entity resolution.

dimensions.name: Code completeness & agent-runnability
dimensions.analysis: No code; a directory page arguably needs none, but a copy-pasteable discovery API call or a sample stream-ID row would raise agent utility.

dimensions.name: Query/intent coverage
dimensions.analysis: Targets "available RWA streams / stream IDs" but delivers none of it statically; no definition, no "how do I verify these onchain" bridge, no troubleshooting.

dimensions.name: Clarity, fluency & terminology consistency
dimensions.analysis: What little text exists is clear and correctly named, but too thin to score higher.

audit.summary: This is a reference directory whose entire reason to exist — the list of RWA stream names, stream IDs, and verifier addresses — is rendered client-side and does not appear in the served HTML (the measured facts show 64 words total, 0 tables, 0 bullets, and the body ends at "Loading..."). A generative engine or coding agent fetching this URL sees three pointer links and a placeholder, not the data it was sent to find. The single biggest opportunity is therefore not prose polish but **server-side rendering (or a static fallback) of the stream table with IDs and addresses in the HTML**; nothing else on this page matters until the payload is retrievable. Metadata scaffolding (valid `TechArticle` + `BreadcrumbList`, canonical URL) is the one relative strength, though its `about`/`keywords` fields are auto-generated noise.

recommendations.title: Render the stream table in static HTML
recommendations.where: `## Mainnet RWA Streams` section (currently ends at "Loading...")
recommendations.issue: `Filter schemaFilter category ... Loading...` — the actual data is JS-only.
recommendations.change: Server-side render (or provide a `<noscript>`/static fallback of) the full table: stream name, asset, stream ID (0x…), feed schema, decimals, and verifier proxy address per network. Ensure it exists in the DOM at fetch time.
recommendations.why: Engines and agents cannot cite or synthesize data that is absent from the retrieved HTML; this is the difference between the page being useless and authoritative for RWA stream lookups. Highest-lift change on the page.

recommendations.title: Add a canonical definition + answer-first opener
recommendations.mapsTo: quotable definitions, answer-first extractability, query coverage
recommendations.where: Directly under the H1, before the tutorial link.
recommendations.issue: Page opens with "To learn how to use Data Streams, see the … tutorial."
recommendations.change: Lead with a self-contained sentence, e.g. "Chainlink RWA Data Streams deliver low-latency price reports for tokenized real-world assets (equities, ETFs, FX). This page lists every available RWA stream, its stream ID, and the verifier proxy address required for onchain verification." Add one line defining "24/5 Equity Streams."
recommendations.why: Gives engines a verbatim-liftable definition and states what the page answers in the first liftable sentence.

recommendations.title: Fix auto-generated schema `about`/`keywords`
recommendations.issue: `about` = "Content about real", "Content about world", "Content about asset" (tokenized fragments); `keywords` = "list, available, Data, Streams, Real, World, Asset, and, their, ID."
recommendations.change: Replace `about` with real entities: `Real World Assets`, `Chainlink Data Streams`, `Tokenized Equities`, `Onchain Verification`. Replace `keywords` with meaningful terms and drop the "and"/"ID." fragments.
recommendations.why: Correct entity metadata aids entity resolution and topical trust; the current split-word Things can mislead parsers. (Lower impact than the retrieval fix — metadata cannot rescue an empty payload.)

recommendations.title: Add symptom/intent-phrased anchors
recommendations.issue: Concept-titled headings only ("Mainnet RWA Streams", "Streams Verifier Network Addresses").
recommendations.change: Add H2/H3s phrased as user queries: "What is the stream ID for [asset]?", "Which verifier proxy address do I use for RWA streams on [network]?", "Are RWA equity streams available 24/7 or 24/5?"
recommendations.why: Devs and agents query by symptom/lookup phrasing; question-shaped headings win retrieval that concept titles lose.

recommendations.title: Provide a real `dateModified` and a discovery-API example
recommendations.where: JSON-LD dates; a new snippet near the discovery link.
recommendations.issue: `datePublished` == `dateModified` (no revision signal); discovery is a bare link.
recommendations.change: Emit an accurate `dateModified`; add a short, tagged, copy-pasteable curl/SDK call to the discovery endpoint that returns RWA streams programmatically.
recommendations.why: Visible freshness raises E-E-A-T; a runnable discovery call gives agents a machine path to the data even before the table renders.

antiPatterns: **Wall-of-placeholder / JS-gated content:** the substantive payload is behind `Loading...` and absent from served HTML.
**Template-noise structured data:** `about` Things like "Content about real" and fragmented `keywords` — auto-generated, not curated.
**Answer-deferring opener:** first line points elsewhere instead of stating what the page delivers.
offPageNotes: Client-side rendering is a site-level framework decision; a prerender/SSR or `<noscript>` fallback for all Data Streams directory pages would fix this class of page, not just this URL.
The auto-generated `about`/`keywords`/date templating appears generator-wide — worth correcting at the docs-pipeline level.
Consider an `llms.txt` and a machine-readable stream registry (JSON/CSV) linked from this page so agents can retrieve IDs/addresses without scraping a rendered table.
